newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba sees 14.2 pct gain in export cigars this year.
newsitem.headline: Cuba sees 14.2 pct gain in export cigars this year.

text.p: Cuba's tobacco industry is on target to produce a total of 70 million cigars for export during 1996, a 14.2 percent increase from the previous year, according to a report in the ruling Communist Party newspaper on Tuesday.
The Granma newspaper quoted Osvaldo Encarnacion, head of the Union of Tobacco Firms, who said the increase reflected hard work by the sector's 3,000 workers.
Cuba produced about 60 million cigars for export in 1995. So far in 1996, the industry has produced 50 million cigars.
Encarnacion said output of cigars for export should reach some 100 million units next year.
As with the rest of the Cuban economy, cigar production slumped from the early 1990s, when tobacco crops suffered amid lack of fertiliser.

The industry's recovery came after Cuba struck deals with several foreign companies, including a two-year-old deal with Tabacalera SA. The Spanish state-owned company agreed to provide credits for input in return for guaranteed exports for the Spanish market.
